_readme: Platform settings: retention, archive storage and integrity, single sign-on and the AI assistant. This file is the baseline and changes by pull request. Retention and archive settings can also be edited in the dashboard under maker-checker (approved changes are laid over this file; see README). Everything that protects the monitor itself (encryption and signing switches, keys, TLS, sign-in mode, the AI endpoint) is deploy-time only: environment variables or a pull request. Secrets are never stored here: keys come from environment variables. status: assumed = a placeholder until the owner confirms it.

retention.source: Placeholder. PCI DSS asks for 12 months of audit-log history with the most recent 3 months immediately available. CBUAE, NESA/IAS and any internal policy may require longer: Compliance sets the real numbers.

sso.source: Design option. Authentication is done by an identity-aware proxy in front of the monitor (Microsoft Entra ID with oauth2-proxy or Application Proxy, or AWS IAM Identity Center behind an ALB). The monitor trusts the identity headers only from the listed proxy addresses and maps directory groups to roles.

ai_assistant.source: Optional, off by default. Calls only the endpoint listed in the register entry SOC_AI_ENDPOINTS, over https, and returns advice only. What may leave the monitor is set by data_policy (default tokenize: credentials and customer identifiers removed, names and addresses replaced by tokens).
ai_assistant.data_policy_note: minimal = structure only; tokenize = default; redact = names sent, secrets and customer identifiers masked; local_full = names and customer identifiers sent, bank-hosted model only, credentials always masked. Deploy-time setting: environment variable or pull request, never the dashboard.
